title: Choose the UniMind access-flow structure
question: The visual world is fixed. Which composition should carry login, verification, recovery, and consent?

options.label: Focused Threshold
options.lineage: a focused academic threshold with a live access ledger
options.thesis: One calm authentication task stays central while the surrounding frame explains exactly what still gates access.
options.viewport: A 254px path rail, one wide credential panel, and a narrow status ledger form a single horizontal threshold.
options.risk: The status ledger must remain useful without exposing private membership details.

options.label: Access Shelf
options.lineage: the approved Focused Rail translated into an account journey
options.thesis: Authentication becomes a four-step academic shelf whose current stage expands without hiding what comes next.
options.viewport: Four aligned stage tiles fill the workspace; Account expands to hold the form while Verify, Consent, and Entry stay visible.
options.risk: A horizontal sequence needs careful mobile scrolling and focus management.

options.label: Policy Desk
options.lineage: an orderly academic desk pairing credentials with commitments
options.thesis: Credentials and the three learner commitments share one working desk, making consent visible before it becomes blocking.
options.viewport: An asymmetric credential panel and three-row commitment ledger sit side by side under one compact progress line.
options.risk: Showing consent beside login can feel dense if the hierarchy is not disciplined.
